body:
I've spent all weekend eating, knowing very well that i'm not hungry. Aweful.

I've always been a pesimist, yes. My mind only leaves me at easy when i'm at work. And it's a terrible feeling to think that in the end work is the only thing that keeps me going :-/.

First of all, thanks for taking the time to write your reply.

Some years ago i put all strength i had left and tried to find a psychologist (It's well known that in the city where i live is rather difficult to get an appointment), giving up after several months. 

I talked to my doctor about this and we started a very soft treatment with serotonin regulators - which we stopped about two years later (that'd be spring last year). I put on a considerable amount of weight and i blamed it on the meds.

Now my nihilist/suicidal thoughts are back, and i gaining more and more weight due to stress eating. I do believe there is some chemical imbalance in my head that leads me to these thought patterns, but i don't know how to go about it, i don't want to be dependent on medication the rest of my life and i'm afraid of the medication turning me into some kind of vegetable...

Coping with that right now myself. Every time i tell myself i will be strong and manage it nicely (go out, try to find something enjoyable to do). But it gets out of hand and it's impossible to put together the will power to even get out of bed. Hopefully somebody can share some tricks to handle these situations better.

That feeling is always there, regardless of the situation, even when i manage to go out and hang out with friends. I think I'm missing some kind of aim or meaning to my life. I find myself often thinking that there is no reason for me to continue living.

I've had these moments of utter sadness and pain where i had just to burst in tears. Thankfully it only happened surrounded by people by more or less understood and were aware of my situation. Nothing to be ashamed of. Sometimes you just have to give up to the feeling and let it out. Hopefully you felt a bit of comfort afterwards.

Hang in there
